message.content:
The crystal adopts the tetragonal space group I-4, number [[param:space_group.number]], with Hall symbol [[param:space_group.hall]]. The originally supplied cell is described in the input frame by lattice parameters a [[param:cell.a]], b [[param:cell.b]], c [[param:cell.c]], with interaxial angles alpha [[param:cell.alpha]], beta [[param:cell.beta]], and gamma [[param:cell.gamma]]. The equal a and b edges together with equal alpha and beta angles are consistent with the tetragonal character of the symmetry, though the input setting is expressed in a nonstandard, oblique coordinate frame. That input cell contains [[param:input.atom_count]] atoms in total, with composition Al [[param:composition.Al]], Cu [[param:composition.Cu]], In [[param:composition.In]], and S [[param:composition.S]].

Mapping this input description onto the standard setting of I-4 requires a change of coordinate frame, given by the transformation matrix [[param:frame.matrix]] together with the origin shift [[param:frame.origin_shift]]. The near-zero off-axis entries of the matrix and the vanishingly small origin shift indicate that this is essentially a rotation and shearing of the basis into the conventional tetragonal axes rather than any physical distortion of the structure. Fractional coordinates in the input frame were rounded to [[param:round_digits]] decimal places.

In the standard setting, the structure is organized into five independent Wyckoff orbits. The aluminum sublattice occupies a single fixed orbit, orbit [[param:orbit.o000.id]] of element [[param:orbit.o000.element]] at Wyckoff position [[param:orbit.o000.wyckoff]], a multiplicity-two site with no free coordinates, whose representative position is at 0, 1/2, 1/4 in the public tabulation. Indium similarly occupies one fixed orbit, orbit [[param:orbit.o001.id]] of element [[param:orbit.o001.element]] at [[param:orbit.o001.wyckoff]], with representative coordinate 0, 0, 1/2 and no adjustable parameters. Copper is split across two distinct fixed orbits: orbit [[param:orbit.o002.id]] of element [[param:orbit.o002.element]] at [[param:orbit.o002.wyckoff]] with representative position 0, 1/2, 3/4, and orbit [[param:orbit.o003.id]] of element [[param:orbit.o003.element]] at [[param:orbit.o003.wyckoff]] located at the origin 0, 0, 0. These four cation orbits, each of multiplicity two, together account for the four metal atoms of the composition, while their fully constrained coordinates mean their arrangement is fixed purely by the symmetry of the space group.

The sulfur sublattice is described by a single general orbit, orbit [[param:orbit.o004.id]] of element [[param:orbit.o004.element]] at Wyckoff position [[param:orbit.o004.wyckoff]]. This is the general position of multiplicity eight with all three fractional coordinates free, and its independent parameters are [[param:orbit.o004.parameters]]. Because the sulfur orbit is generated by the full symmetry of the group, the eight symmetry-equivalent sulfur sites of the general position reproduce the four sulfur atoms of the primitive input description under the body-centered tetragonal lattice.

Finally, the idealized orbit expansion requires small precision corrections to match the input exactly; these are genuine deviations of the input sites from the idealized backbone, not features of the ideal structure. One expanded sulfur site, [[param:correction.c000.site_id]] of element [[param:correction.c000.element]], is displaced by [[param:correction.c000.delta]], a shift confined to the x direction. A second sulfur site, [[param:correction.c001.site_id]] of element [[param:correction.c001.element]], carries the correction [[param:correction.c001.delta]], confined instead to the y direction. Both displacements are on the order of one part in a million of a unit-cell edge, so the idealized symmetry description captures the geometry almost exactly, with only these minute residuals separating it from the supplied input coordinates.
